meta.title: GATE DA 2027 Practice Book
meta.note: Unofficial practice book. Layout follows standard GATE / Made Easy unit-then-solutions books. Stems follow official DA 2024-2026 habits with new numbers and wording. Official PYQs are not copied. Mocks use the latest confirmed paper: 65 Q, 100 marks, 3 hours.

questions.stem: A lab has 8 data scientists and 6 engineers. A review panel of 5 is formed with at least 2 engineers. The number of possible panels is
questions.sol: Count panels by number of engineers e=2,3,4,5: C(8,5-e)C(6,e). Sum equals 1526.

questions.stem: A finite sample space Omega = {omega1, omega2, omega3} has P({omega1})=0.2 and P({omega2})=0.5. Which assignment is the only one compatible with Kolmogorov axioms?
Events A,B satisfy P(A)=0.4, P(B)=0.5. They CANNOT be both mutually exclusive and independent because
options: independence needs P(A n B)=0.2 while exclusivity needs P(A n B)=0
they would have to be the same event
questions.sol: Independent nonempty-probability events have positive intersection probability P(A)P(B)>0, hence cannot be disjoint.

questions.stem: Two factories ship phones. Factory F1 ships 2000 phones with 2% defective; F2 ships 3000 phones with 6% defective. A phone is drawn uniformly from the 5000 and is defective. P(it came from F1) is closest to
questions.sol: Defectives: 40 from F1, 180 from F2. P(F1|D)=40/220 ~ 0.182.

Which statement is TRUE for finite-variance random variables?
options: Independent => Cov=0, but Cov=0 need not imply independent
Corr is defined even if Var(X)=0
questions.sol: Independence implies uncorrelatedness; the converse fails. Additivity of variance needs uncorrelatedness. Correlation needs positive variances.

questions.sol: Poisson: mean=var=lambda. Geometric mean 1/p, variance (1-p)/p^2, equal only for special p (p= (sqrt(5)-1)/2 not generic). DA 2024 used Poisson+N(0,1); this pairs Poisson with Geometric instead.

Uniform on the segment x+y=1, 0<x<1 (hence dependent)
questions.sol: Y is a deterministic function of X, supported on the line x+y=1.

questions.stem: A waiting-time model is called memoryless if P(X>s+t | X>s)=P(X>t). Which option lists memoryless laws?
questions.sol: The memoryless laws on R+ and on N are Exponential and Geometric.

questions.sol: Poisson mean=var. N(0,4) has variance 4, not 1..)

questions.stem: A fair three-sided spinner (labels A,B,C) is spun 5 times independently. P(exactly 2 A's, 2 B's, 1 C) equals
In hypothesis testing, a Type I error is
options: rejecting H0 when H0 is false
computing a CI instead of a test
failing to reject H0 when H0 is false
rejecting H0 when H0 is true
questions.sol: Type I = false rejection; Type II = false non-rejection.

questions.stem: i.i.d. Xi with finite mean mu. The weak law of large numbers states that Xbar_n converges to mu
options: only when the Xi are Normal
almost surely only if the Xi are bounded, and never in probability otherwise
questions.sol: WLLN is convergence in probability. SLLN is a.s. (under slightly stronger hypotheses).

questions.stem: Seven distinct faculty sit around a circular conference table. Two particular faculty refuse to sit next to each other. The number of distinct seating arrangements, treating rotations as identical, is
questions.sol: Circular arrangements of 7 are 6!. Treat the pair as glued: 2*5!. Subtract to get 6!-2*5! = 480.

questions.stem: For events A,B with P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.7, the smallest possible value of P(A n B) is
questions.sol: Frechet bound: P(A n B) >= P(A)+P(B)-1 = 0.3.

questions.stem: Two fair coins are tossed independently. Let A = first coin is heads, B = second coin is heads, C = the two coins show different faces. Then
options: A,B,C are pairwise independent but not mutually independent
questions.sol: Pairwise: each pair has P=1/4 = (1/2)(1/2). But A n B n C is empty (two heads cannot differ), so P(A n B n C)=0 != 1/8.

questions.stem: A joint table of (Job type J, Delay D) is: intern: on-time 20, delayed 10; full-time: on-time 40, delayed 30 (counts). Assuming uniform over the 100 jobs, P(delayed | intern) equals
A binary classifier for a rare class with prevalence 0.01 has sensitivity 0.99 and specificity 0.99. Which claims are correct?
options: P(class=1 | predicted 1) is far below 0.99 because of the low prevalence
questions.sol: PPV is pulled down by the 99:1 prior odds. FPR=1-specificity=0.01. Specificity is P(predicted 0 | class=0), not the FPR.

questions.stem: Let F be the CDF of an integer-valued exam score. Which property must F satisfy?
options: right-continuous and non-decreasing, with jumps at atoms of the law
questions.sol: CDFs are always right-continuous and non-decreasing; discrete laws add jumps. They need not be left-continuous or strictly increasing.

questions.stem: X~Binomial(n=6, p=1/3). Which identities hold?
options: X is approximately N(2, 4/3) with no error even for n=6 (exact, not approximate)
questions.sol: Mean, variance and empty-success probability are exact. CLT is an approximation, not an identity for n=6.

questions.stem: A 4x4 matrix of i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) entries. P(the first row sums to 2 AND the first column sums to 2). The overlapping (1,1) entry is shared. This probability, rounded to three decimals, is _____.
questions.sol: Condition on a11. Each case multiplies two independent Binomial(3,1/2) probabilities: 0.5*(3/8)^2 + 0.5*(3/8)^2 = (3/8)^2 = 0.140625 ~ 0.141.

options: non-decreasing and right-continuous with limits 0 at -inf and 1 at +inf

questions.stem: The spacings of n i.i.d. Uniform(0,1) order statistics are distributed as
options: normalised i.i.d. exponentials (Dirichlet(1,..,1) on the simplex)
questions.sol: Classic fact: n+1 spacings including ends are like n+1 i.i.d. exp / sum.

options: heavier tails and a peak a little lower at 0
questions.sol: t is symmetric about 0 with polynomial tails; as nu->inf it approaches N(0,1).

questions.stem: Dice: a fair six-sided die is rolled 4 times. The number of outcome tuples with each of four distinct faces (a permutation of four different numbers) is P(6,4)= _____.
Power of a level-alpha test against a particular alternative is
From a standard 52-card deck, a 5-card hand is dealt. The number of hands that are flushes (all five cards of one suit, including straight flushes) is
questions.sol: Choose suit in 4 ways then 5 ranks from 13: 4*C(13,5)=5148. (Straight-flush exclusion is not asked.)

questions.stem: For events A,B with P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.7, the largest possible value of P(A n B) is
If A and B are mutually exclusive and P(A)>0, P(B)>0, then P(A|B) equals
questions.sol: A n B is empty so the conditional probability is 0. They are dependent.

options: Geometric starting at 0 with success probability 1-q
questions.sol: This is the Geometric(number of failures) law.

questions.stem: X~Exponential with mean 1/ln 2. Let Y=floor(X). Then P(Y=ell) = (1-q) q^ell for ell=0,1,2,... The value of q is
questions.sol: P(Y>=ell)=P(X>=ell)=e^{-ell ln 2}=2^{-ell}, a geometric ratio q=1/2.

questions.stem: Student's t with one degree of freedom is equal in law to which named distribution?
questions.sol: Student t with 1 df is Cauchy.

questions.stem: Given Y=y, X is N(y, 1), and Y is N(0,1). Then the joint of (X,Y) is
questions.sol: E[X|Y]=Y so Cov(X,Y)=Var(Y)=1, Var(X)=E[Var(X|Y)]+Var(E[X|Y])=1+1=2. Bivariate Gaussian.

questions.stem: The Lindeberg-Lévy CLT requires which of the following as a sufficient set of hypotheses?
questions.sol: Classical CLT: i.i.d. and finite variance. Cauchy has no mean.

A z-test of H0: p=0.5 vs H1: p>0.5 with n=100, p-hat=0.58 has z=(0.58-0.5)/sqrt(0.5*0.5/100)=1.6. Using z_{0.05}=1.645, at 5% one-sided we
questions.sol: The statistic falls just short of the 5% critical value.

questions.sol: Two estimated means and one pooled variance: n1+n2-2.

Which statements are correct about GATE-style hypothesis tests?
options: z-tests require a known sigma (or a large-sample plug-in)
A chi^2 GoF statistic is always exactly chi^2 even for n=5 sparse cells
Failing to reject H0 does not prove H0 is true
A small p-value is evidence against H0 (under the modelling assumptions)
questions.sol: p-values are not proof of H0. Chi^2 is an approximation requiring adequate expected counts.

questions.stem: A reading list is formed by choosing 3 books from 5 distinct ML texts, 4 distinct systems texts, and 3 distinct theory texts, with at least one ML text. The number of lists (order does not matter) is
questions.sol: Total C(12,3) minus lists with no ML book C(7,3) = 220-35=185.

questions.stem: Consider statements about a probability measure P on a sample space Omega. (i) P(empty set)=0. (ii) If A subset B then P(A) <= P(B). Which option is correct?
questions.sol: Both are standard consequences of Kolmogorov axioms (monotonicity and empty-set probability).

questions.stem: Let A,B be independent. Which one is NOT necessarily true?
questions.sol: Independence is preserved by complements, but the union formula without subtracting the product is exclusivity, not independence.

questions.stem: X and Y are independent. X is uniform on {1,2} and Y is uniform on {0,1}. Then P(X+Y=2) equals
questions.sol: Favourable independent pairs: (1,1) and (2,0), each with probability 1/4, total 1/2.

questions.stem: In a mailbox, 30% of messages are spam. A filter tags spam with probability 0.90 and tags ham as spam with probability 0.05. Given a tagged message, P(spam) equals _____ (two decimals).
Let Z = a + bX + error with E[error]=0 and E[error(X-E[X])]=0. Given E[X]=1, Var(X)=4, Cov(Z,X)=-2 and E[Z]=3, the pair (a,b) is
Five integers from 0 to 20 (repetitions allowed) have mean 10, median 12, and a unique mode 14. Which statement is TRUE?
options: The unique mode must be the median
After sorting x1<=x2<=x3<=x4<=x5 we must have x3=12, the unique mode 14 appears at least twice, and the mean constraint is  x1+...+x5=50
Such a sample is impossible because mode 14 > median 12
questions.sol: Median is the middle of five. A unique mode 14 must occur more often than others and at least twice, which is compatible with median 12 if 14 occupies the upper end. Mean 10 is a sum constraint, not impossibility.

questions.stem: X~Uniform(-1,1). Given X=x, Y is Uniform(x^2-0.2, x^2+0.2). Then Corr(X,Y) equals
questions.sol: E[Y|X]=X^2, so E[XY]=E[X^3]=0 and E[X]=0, hence Cov=0.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a valid PMF on {0,1,2}?
questions.sol: Must be non-negative and sum to 1. Only (0.2,0.3,0.5) works.

questions.stem: A basketball player hits a free throw with probability 0.6 independently. In 5 attempts, P(exactly 4 hits) equals _____ (rounded to three decimals).
Let N~Poisson(lambda) with lambda>0. Which are true?
options: N takes values in (0, inf) with a density
questions.sol: Poisson is a discrete law on {0,1,2,...}; it has no density on the line. The factorial-moment and MGF formulae hold.

questions.stem: If F is the CDF of a continuous r.v. with density f, then almost everywhere
questions.sol: Fundamental theorem: the density is the derivative of the CDF.

questions.stem: Two independent Uniform(0,1) r.v.s U,V. P(U+V<=1) equals _____ (one decimal).
questions.sol: Lower triangle of the unit square, area 1/2.

questions.stem: Let X~Exponential(rate=lambda). Which are true?
options: The MGF is lambda/(lambda-t) for t<lambda
questions.sol: Memoryless, second moment 2/l^2, MGF formula. A continuous law has P(X=0)=0.

questions.sol: The t pivot has n-1 degrees of freedom.

questions.stem: Joint density f(x,y)=e^{-x-y} for x>0,y>0. Then f_{X|Y}(x|y) for x>0 equals e^{-x} (does not depend on y). The value of f_{X|Y}(1|5) rounded to two decimals is _____.
questions.sol: Independence: conditional density is e^{-x}, so e^{-1}~0.37.

questions.stem: A de Moivre-Laplace application: n=16 independent Bernoulli(1/2). Approximate P(S=8) using a continuity correction as P(7.5<S*<8.5) where S*~N(8,4). This equals Phi((8.5-8)/2)-Phi((7.5-8)/2) = Phi(0.25)-Phi(-0.25). Using Phi(0.25)~0.5987 the approximation rounded to two decimals is
Which statement about a 95% CI for mu is correct (repeated sampling interpretation)?
options: About 95% of such random intervals contain the true mu
Width does not depend on n
The interval always contains Xbar at an endpoint
P(mu in this already-computed interval)=0.95 as a posterior
questions.sol: Frequentist coverage is a property of the procedure, not of one realised interval as a posterior probability.

questions.stem: n=100, sigma=10, Xbar=103, H0: mu=100 vs H1: mu != 100, alpha=0.05, z_crit=1.96. Which are true?
options: The 95% z-interval for mu is centred at 100
questions.sol: SE=1, z=3>1.96 so reject. The CI is centred at Xbar=103, not at the H0 value.

questions.stem: n=9, Xbar=4, s=3, H0: mu=2. The t statistic equals _____ (integer).
A Pearson chi-squared test of independence is run on an r x c table with large n. Which are true?
options: The test requires the two classification variables to be Normal
Expected cell counts use the product of fitted marginals
A large statistic (with small p) is evidence against independence
questions.sol: It is a categorical test; Normality of the labels is not assumed. Expected counts are n * p_row * p_col under independence.

questions.stem: Matching: Column P = memoryless continuous; Q = mean=variance; R = limits of t_n. Column 2: 1 Exponential, 2 Poisson, 3 N(0,1). The correct match is
questions.sol: Exponential is memoryless, Poisson has mean=var, t_n -> N(0,1).

questions.stem: In a level-alpha two-sided z-test of H0: mu=mu0 (sigma known), which are true?
options: Failing to reject H0 proves mu=mu0
Power is a function of the true mu, n, sigma and alpha
Type I error probability is alpha when H0 is true (under the Normal/CLT model)
p-value < alpha is the same decision as rejecting at level alpha
questions.sol: Standard Neyman-Pearson facts. Non-rejection is not a proof of H0.

questions.stem: Let S be a 4-element set. The number of functions f: S -> S that are bijections AND satisfy f(f(x))=x for every x in S (involutions that are permutations) is
questions.sol: Count involutions in S_4: the identity, 6 transpositions, and 3 products of two disjoint transpositions, total 10.

questions.stem: Two events A and B satisfy P(A u B)=P(A)+P(B). This equality holds if and only if
questions.sol: Additivity of P on a union requires the intersection to be null (almost surely disjoint).

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice independently. Let D be the event that the sum is 7 and E the event that the first roll is 3. Then P(D n E) equals
questions.sol: D n E = {(3,4)} only, probability 1/36. Also P(D)=6/36, P(E)=1/6, product 1/36, so D and E are independent.

questions.stem: For a joint density f_{X,Y}(x,y), the conditional density f_{X|Y}(x|y) equals (when f_Y(y)>0)
questions.sol: Definition of conditional density: joint over marginal.

questions.stem: Plant A makes 70% of chips (defect rate 1%); plant B makes the rest (defect rate 4%). A randomly chosen chip is defective. P(it came from plant B) equals _____ (two decimals).
If E[X|Y]=c almost surely for a constant c, then
options: X is independent of Y necessarily
questions.sol: Tower gives E[X]=c. Also E[XY]=E[E[X|Y] Y]=c E[Y] so Cov=0. Independence and degeneracy need not hold.

questions.stem: A data set of n=5 values has sum 20 and sum of squares 100. The population variance (divide by n) is _____.
The correlation matrix of a non-degenerate random vector must be
options: symmetric positive semidefinite with ones on the diagonal
questions.sol: Corr = D^{-1/2} Cov D^{-1/2} is a Gram matrix, hence SPD/PSD, with unit diagonal.

questions.stem: Let X be integer-valued with CDF F. Which statements are correct?
questions.sol: Standard discrete CDF facts. F is right-continuous, not left-continuous.

questions.stem: A 10-question MCQ is guessed independently with 4 options each. P(at least one correct) = 1-(3/4)^10. This value rounded to two decimals is _____.
Calls arrive as Poisson with mean 3 per minute. P(no call in a given minute) equals e^{-3}. Rounded to three decimals this is _____.
Let f be a PDF on R. Which properties MUST hold?
questions.sol: Non-negativity and unit integral. Densities may exceed 1 (e.g. Uniform(0,0.1)) and need not be continuous.

questions.stem: Waiting times W1, W2 are i.i.d. Exponential(rate=1). Which are true?
questions.sol: Min of independent exponentials adds rates. Sum is Erlang. Symmetry gives P(W1<W2)=1/2.

questions.stem: Independent X~N(1,4) and Y~N(2,9). Then X+Y is
questions.sol: Sum of independent Gaussians is Gaussian with added means and variances.

questions.stem: Which are true for Student's t_nu as nu -> infinity?
options: t_nu converges in distribution to N(0,1)
the variance of t_nu (for nu>2) tends to 1
P(|t_nu|>2) tends to P(|Z|>2) for Z~N(0,1)
questions.sol: Standard limit of t. Variance is nu/(nu-2) -> 1.

questions.stem: Joint density f(x,y)=8xy on 0<y<x<1. The conditional f_{Y|X}(y|x) for 0<y<x is 2y/x^2. Hence f_{Y|X}(0.2|0.5) equals _____.
Which quantity is asymptotically N(0,1) under i.i.d. finite-variance sampling, with mu, sigma known?
If a 95% CI for mu is (2.1, 3.7), then a two-sided t-test of H0: mu=3 at level 5%
options: is inapplicable because 3 is an integer
questions.sol: 3 lies inside the interval, so H0 is not rejected at 5%.

questions.stem: A one-sided z-test has z=1.64. Using Phi(1.64)~0.9495, the p-value P(Z>1.64) rounded to two decimals is _____.
A die is rolled 60 times. Under fairness E_i=10 for each face. Observed counts 8,12,9,11,7,13. The Pearson chi^2 statistic sum (O-E)^2/E equals _____ (one decimal).
Let phi be convex and X integrable so that E[phi(X)] exists. Jensen's inequality states that
questions.sol: Convex: phi of mean <= mean of phi. Variance identity is the square case.

questions.stem: There are 6 distinct courses. The number of ways to assign each course a slot in {morning, afternoon, evening} so that every slot is used at least once is
questions.sol: Onto functions from 6 courses to 3 slots: 3^6 - C(3,1)2^6 + C(3,2)= 729-192+3=540.

Consider (i) mutually exclusive events with positive probability are dependent; (ii) Cov(X,Y)=0 always implies X,Y independent. Which is correct?
questions.sol: (i) holds because P(A n B)=0 != P(A)P(B). Uncorrelated does not imply independent (classic counterexamples).

questions.stem: X,Y have joint density f(x,y)=1 on the unit square (0,1)^2. Then X and Y are
questions.sol: f factors as 1*1 and each marginal is Uniform(0,1).

questions.stem: Tomorrow rains with probability 0.2. A forecast says 'rain' with probability 0.8 if it will rain and with probability 0.1 if it will not. Given a 'rain' forecast, P(rain) equals _____ (two decimals).
A biased coin with P(H)=1/3 is tossed independently until two consecutive heads appear. The expected number of tosses is
The interquartile range of the ordered sample 2,4,6,8,10,12,14 is Q3-Q1. With Q1=4 and Q3=12 (seven-point convention using medians of halves excluding the overall median), IQR equals _____.
Let X,Y be independent, X~Bernoulli(0.4), Y~Normal(0, 25). Then Var((2X-1)Y) equals
questions.sol: (2X-1)= +/-1 with probabilities 0.4 and 0. (2X-1)^2=1, E[Y]=0 so second term 0, E[Y^2]=25. Twist on DA 2026 Q44 (which used p=0.3, var 100).

questions.stem: X takes values in {0,1,2} with p=(0.2,0.5,0.3). Which are true?
questions.sol: E[X]=0.5+0.6=1.1. CDF at 1.7 includes 0 and 1. A discrete law has P(X=1.7)=0.

questions.stem: Four independent servers fail with probability 0.1 each. P(exactly two fail) equals _____ (rounded to four decimals).
A Poisson process has rate 5 per hour. The expected waiting time (in hours) until the first event is _____ (one decimal).
f(x)=3x^2 on (0,1). Then Var(X) equals _____ (four decimals).
X is Exponential with mean 5. If P(X>5)=e^{-1}, then P(X>10 | X>5) equals _____ (rounded to two decimals).
The 68-95-99.7 rule says that about 95% of N(mu,sigma^2) mass lies in
questions.sol: Two-sigma interval is the 95% heuristic (more precisely 1.96).

questions.stem: A one-sample t-test is applied to n=9 allegedly i.i.d. Normal observations. Which are true?
options: Under H0 the t statistic has 8 degrees of freedom
The t critical value is smaller than the z critical value for the same tail probability
If sigma were known one would use a z-test instead
Heavy-tailed true data (not Normal, small n) make the nominal 5% level untrustworthy
questions.sol: t_{n-1} is heavier-tailed than N(0,1), so |t|_{crit} > z_crit. Normality matters for small n.

questions.stem: X~Uniform(0,1), Y|X=x ~ Uniform(0,x). Then E[Y] equals _____ (two decimals).
Let X1,...,Xn be i.i.d. with mean mu and finite variance sigma^2>0. Which are true for large n?
options: Xbar converges in probability to mu (WLLN)
Xbar is exactly t_{n-1} for every n, even if the Xi are Uniform
questions.sol: CLT and WLLN apply. The exact t law needs Gaussian data and an independent sample sd in the denominator, not the raw mean.

questions.stem: n i.i.d. N(mu, sigma^2) with sigma known. A 95% z-interval I_n = Xbar +/- 1.96 sigma/sqrt(n). Which are true?
options: P_mu(I_n contains mu)=0.95 for every n>=1
Replacing 1.96 by 2.58 produces a 99% interval of the same centre
The interval is a posterior 95% credible set under every prior
The length of I_n tends to 0 as n tends to inf
questions.sol: Exact Gaussian z-interval has exact coverage. Length shrinks. Larger z widens a still-centred interval.

questions.stem: A 2x3 contingency table (independence, no estimated extra parameters beyond margins) has chi^2 degrees of freedom equal to _____.
Assume the MGF M(t)=E[e^{tX}] exists in a neighbourhood of 0. Then M'(0) equals
questions.sol: The first derivative of the MGF at 0 is the mean.

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed until the first head appears, but at most 4 tosses are made. The size of the sample space if an outcome is recorded as a finite string over {H,T} (stopping at H or at 4 tosses) is
questions.sol: Outcomes: H, TH, TTH, TTTH, TTTT. Five atoms.

questions.stem: Let A,B be events in a probability space. Which of the following are ALWAYS true?
options: P(A u B) = P(A)+P(B)-P(A n B)
questions.sol: Inclusion-exclusion and complement are axioms/theorems; Boole's inequality always holds. Product formula needs independence.

questions.stem: A and B are independent with 0 < P(A),P(B) < 1. Which statements MUST be true?
questions.sol: Independence is the product formula, which implies P(A|B)=P(A) and the inclusion-exclusion form. Disjointness would force a zero product, a contradiction.

questions.stem: A joint PMF is given by the table X\Y | 0 1 2 and rows X=0: 0.05, 0.10, 0.15; X=1: 0.10, 0.20, 0.40. Which statement is TRUE?
options: The table already fails to be a PMF because the entries sum to more than 1
X and Y are independent because no cell is zero
questions.sol: Row X=1 sums to 0.70, so the conditional is 0.40/0.70. Entries sum to 1.00 so it is a PMF; independence would need a product structure (fails: 0.05 vs 0.15*0.30? P(X=0)=0.30, P(Y=0)=0.15, product 0.045 != 0.05).

questions.stem: Three drawers: D1 has 3 gold 1 silver coins; D2 has 1 gold 3 silver; D3 has 2 gold 2 silver. A drawer is chosen uniformly. A gold coin is drawn. P(drawer was D1 | gold) equals _____ (two decimals).
X,Y square-integrable. Which identities always hold?
options: E[X|Y]=E[X] almost surely even when X and Y are dependent
E[X g(Y)]=E[E[X|Y] g(Y)] for bounded g
questions.sol: Tower property, law of total variance, and the defining projection property. E[X|Y]=E[X] is independence-like (mean independence), not automatic.

questions.stem: Five exam scores have mean 12. After a sixth score 18 is included, the new mean is _____ (one decimal).
Which claims are correct?
options: Var(X+Y) <= (sd X + sd Y)^2 always (finite variances)
Corr(aX+b, cY+d) = sign(ac) Corr(X,Y) for a,c != 0
questions.sol: Cauchy-Schwarz gives |rho|<=1 and the triangle inequality for sd. Affine transforms pick up the sign of the slopes. Cov(X,X)=Var(X), not 0.

questions.stem: X has PMF P(X=-1)=0.2, P(X=0)=0.3, P(X=2)=0.5. Then Var(X) equals _____ (two decimals).
A fair die is rolled 5 times. P(exactly two sixes) equals _____ (rounded to three decimals).
Density f(x)=2x on (0,1). The median m satisfies F(m)=1/2, so m equals _____ (rounded to two decimals).
Two independent Exponential(rate=1) clocks. The expected time until the first rings is _____ (one decimal).
questions.sol: Minimum of two i.i.d. Exp(1) is Exp(2), mean 1/2.

questions.stem: Z~N(0,1) with pdf g and CDF G; Y~t_1 with pdf h and CDF H. Let c>0 satisfy g(c)=h(c). Which statement is TRUE?
options: G(0)=H(0)=1/2 because both densities are even
t_1 has lighter tails than N(0,1)
G is the CDF of a Uniform(0,1)
questions.sol: Both laws are symmetric about 0 so both CDFs equal 1/2 at 0. t_1 (Cauchy) has heavier tails.

questions.stem: Var of t_nu for nu=4 equals nu/(nu-2) = _____.
Bivariate density f(x,y)= (x+y)/8 on 0<x<2, 0<y<2. The marginal f_X(1) equals int_0^2 (1+y)/8 dy = _____ (three decimals).
n=25 i.i.d. Uniform(0,12), which have variance 12. Then sd of Xbar is _____ (two decimals).
questions.sol: Var Uniform(0,12)=144/12=12, sd of mean = sqrt(12)/5 ~ 0.693. Report 0.69.

questions.stem: n=16, sigma=8, Xbar=50, z_{0.025}=1.96. Half-width of the 95% z-interval is 1.96*8/4 = _____ (two decimals).
Two independent Exp(1) r.v.s X,Y. Then X/(X+Y) is distributed as
questions.sol: For i.i.d. Exp, the normalised first is Uniform (Dirichlet/Beta(1,1)).

questions.stem: Let S be a finite n-set. Which counting formulae are correct?
options: The number of 2-element sequences with repetition from S is C(n,2)
The number of k-subsets is C(n,k)
The number of permutations of S is n!
The number of injections from a k-set to S is P(n,k)=n!/(n-k)! for k<=n
questions.sol: Sequences with repetition: n^2, not C(n,2). C(n,2) counts unordered pairs.

questions.stem: Let A,B be events with 0<P(A)<1 and 0<P(B)<1. Which statements MUST be true?
questions.sol: Monotonicity gives the two inequalities. Conditioning on B, A and A^c partition the space. Bayes does not force P(A|B)=P(B|A).

questions.stem: Which constructions yield independent events (assuming fair independent tosses of two coins)?
options: A = first heads, B = coins show equal faces
A = empty event, B = any event
A = first heads, B = second heads
A = first heads, B = at least one head  (these are dependent)
questions.sol: First and second heads are independent; first heads and equality: P both = 1/4 = (1/2)(1/2). Empty event is independent of everything. 'At least one head' is dependent on first heads.

questions.stem: Let f_{X,Y}(x,y)=e^{-x-y} for x>0, y>0. Then X and Y are
questions.sol: The joint factors as e^{-x} e^{-y} on the positive quadrant.

questions.stem: A box contains two coins: one fair and one two-headed. A coin is picked at random and flipped; it shows heads. P(the coin is two-headed | heads) equals _____ (two decimals).
Y is Uniform on {1,2,3}. Given Y=y, X is Uniform on {1,...,y} (discrete). Then E[X] equals _____ (rounded to two decimals).
For {4, 8, 10, 12, 16}, the population standard deviation (divide by n, not n-1) equals _____ (two decimals).
X,Y have finite positive variances. Which are true?
options: Corr(X,Y)=0 iff X and Y are independent
Corr(X,Y)=1 iff Y=a+bX a.s. for some b>0
questions.sol: Cauchy-Schwarz: |rho|=1 iff linear relation a.s. with the sign of b. Zero correlation is weaker than independence.

questions.stem: X ~ Geometric(p=1/3) on {1,2,...}. Then P(X>4 | X>2) equals P(X>2) by memorylessness, and P(X>2)=(2/3)^2. The conditional probability equals _____ (rounded to two decimals).
Eight emails, each independently spam with probability 1/4. P(exactly 2 spam) equals _____ (rounded to four decimals).
Let X~N(0,1). Which are true?
questions.sol: Standard normal is symmetric about 0, odd moments vanish, P(X>0)=1/2.

questions.stem: Let Y ~ N(0,1) and, given Y=y, let X ~ N(y, 1). Then Var(X) equals _____.
Sum S_n of n i.i.d. with mean 0 variance 1. Approximate P(S_n / sqrt(n) <= 0) for large n is _____ (one decimal).
questions.sol: The standardised sum is approx N(0,1).

questions.stem: To have a 95% z-interval half-width at most 0.5 when sigma=2 and z=1.96, the smallest integer n satisfying n >= (1.96*2/0.5)^2 is _____.
A Poisson process of rate 2 is observed for time 3. The count N(3) is distributed as
questions.sol: Poisson process counts are Poisson(rate * time).

questions.stem: The number of onto (surjective) functions from a 4-element feature-index set to a 3-element label set {red, green, blue} is _____.
Three events A,B,C are pairwise disjoint with P(A)=0.1, P(B)=0.25, P(C)=0.15. Then P(A u B u C) equals _____ (two decimals).
A fair coin is tossed twice independently. Let H1 = first toss heads, Eq = both tosses equal, Xor = tosses differ. Which of the following pairs are independent?
questions.sol: P(H1 n Eq)=P(HH)=1/4=P(H1)P(Eq). Same for Xor. But Eq and Xor are complementary, hence disjoint with positive probability, so dependent.

questions.stem: A survey of 80 students yields the counts (laptop, yes-coffee)=30, (laptop, no-coffee)=10, (no-laptop, yes-coffee)=20, (no-laptop, no-coffee)=20. P(coffee | laptop) equals

A server crash is due to hardware with prior 0.3, otherwise software. A diagnostic flags hardware with probability 0.9 if hardware and 0.2 if software. Given a hardware flag, P(true hardware fault) equals _____ (two decimals).
A fair die is rolled. If the face is even, a fair coin is tossed once and X=number of heads; if odd, the coin is tossed twice and X=number of heads. E[X] equals _____ (two decimals).
z-score of a value 82 when the attribute has mean 70 and sd 8 equals _____ (one decimal).
Var(X)=4, Var(Y)=9, Corr(X,Y)=0.5. Then Var(2X-Y) equals _____.
X takes values 1,2,3,4 each with probability 1/4. Then P(X <= 2.5) equals _____ (two decimals).
A batter gets a hit with probability 0.3 independently in 8 at-bats. P(at least one hit)=1-(0.7)^8. Rounded to two decimals this is _____.
X~N(2, 16) and Z=(X-2)/4. Which are true?
options: Var(X+Z)=16+1 because X and Z are independent
questions.sol: Z is an affine function of X, hence perfectly dependent with X; Var(X+Z)=Var(1.25 X - 0.5) is not 17.

questions.stem: n=9 Normal observations, s=3, t_{8, 0.025}=2.306. Half-width of the 95% t-interval is 2.306*s/sqrt(n) = _____ (two decimals).
Let I_A be the 0-1 indicator of an event A on a probability space. Then E[I_A] equals
questions.sol: Fundamental bridge: expectation of an indicator is the probability.

questions.stem: Five boys and four girls sit in a row so that no two girls are adjacent. The number of seating arrangements of these 9 distinct people is _____.
questions.sol: Seat boys first: 5! ways, creating 6 gaps; choose 4 gaps for girls: C(6,4)*4!. Product is 43200.

questions.stem: A sample space has 8 equally likely outcomes. Event A contains 3 of them. P(A^c) equals _____ (three decimals).
Three independent alarms each fail with probability 0.2. The probability that at least one works is _____ (three decimals).
A 2x2 joint PMF on {0,1}x{0,1} has all four cells equal to 1/4. Which are true?
options: X and Y are independent Bernoulli(1/2)

questions.stem: An oil well is wet with prior 0.4. A seismic test is positive with probability 0.85 if wet and 0.25 if dry. Given a positive test, P(wet) equals _____ (two decimals).
N~Poisson(3) and given N=n, X is Binomial(n, 0.5) (X=0 if n=0). Then E[X] equals _____ (one decimal).
X is Uniform on {1,2,3} and Y=X^2. Then Cov(X,Y)=E[X^3]-E[X]E[X^2]. This covariance equals _____ (rounded to two decimals).

A login succeeds with probability 0.4 independently. In 5 attempts, P(first success occurs on the 5th attempt) equals _____ (rounded to four decimals). (This is a geometric probability, not a binomial count.)
If X~N(0, sigma^2), the MGF E[e^{tX}] equals exp(sigma^2 t^2 / 2). For sigma=2 and t=1 the MGF equals e^k with k=_____.
A 95% z-interval is built from n=16, sigma=8, Xbar=50 and z_{0.025}=1.96. Its lower endpoint is _____ (two decimals).
Five i.i.d. N(0,1) r.v.s. Let S = X1^2+...+X5^2 and T = sqrt(5) Xbar. Which is TRUE?
options: S ~ chi^2_5 and T^2 ~ chi^2_1, and S-T^2 ~ chi^2_4 independent of T
questions.sol: Cochran: sample ss splits into n(Xbar)^2 ~ chi^2_1 and residual chi^2_{n-1}, independent.

questions.stem: The number of onto functions from a 5-element domain to a 3-element codomain is _____.
Three independent alarms each fail with probability 0.1. The probability that all three fail is _____ (three decimals).
Joint PMF p(x,y)=(x+y)/21 for x=1,2 and y=1,2,3. Then P(X=2) equals _____ (rounded to two decimals).

City buses are 80% blue and 20% green. A witness identifies a bus as green; the witness is correct 75% of the time (and otherwise names the other colour). P(bus is green | identified green) equals _____ (two decimals).
N~Poisson(4) and given N=n, S is the sum of n i.i.d. Uniform{1,2} (S=0 if n=0). E[S] equals _____ (integer).
A 2D sample of 4 points: (1,2), (2,4), (3,6), (4,8). The (Pearson) sample correlation is _____.
questions.sol: Y=2X exactly on the sample, so r=1.

questions.stem: A shopper buys a warranty on a visit with probability 0.3, independently across 7 visits. The variance of the number of warranties sold is _____ (two decimals).
The matrix [[4, 3], [3, 1]] is claimed as a covariance matrix. This claim is
options: true, because the diagonal is positive
false, because a 2x2 covariance must be PSD and 4*1-9=-5<0
questions.sol: Symmetric is necessary but not sufficient: eigenvalues must be >=0, equivalently det>=0 here.

questions.stem: How many 5-digit integers (no leading zero) can be formed using digits 0-9 if repetition is not allowed?
questions.sol: First digit: 9 choices (1-9). Then 9 remaining (including 0) for the second, then 8,7,6. Product 27216.

questions.stem: Joint PMF: P(X=0,Y=0)=0.15, P(X=0,Y=1)=0.25, P(X=1,Y=0)=0.20, P(X=1,Y=1)=0.40. Then Cov(X,Y) equals _____ (two decimals).
A malware scanner flags 98% of infected files and 4% of clean files. Prevalence of infection is 1%. Given a flag, P(infected) equals _____ (two decimals).
A gambler starts with 0. Each step a fair coin adds +1 or -1. Let T be the first time the fortune is +2 or -2. E[T] equals _____ (integer).
questions.sol: Simple symmetric random walk hitting time of +/-a from 0 has mean a^2=4.

questions.stem: A byte is 8 independent bits, each equal to 1 with probability 0.5. P(the byte has even parity), i.e. even number of 1s, equals _____ (two decimals).
questions.sol: For a fair independent bits, even and odd parity are equally likely: 0.50.

questions.stem: Negative-binomial flavour: independent Bernoulli(p=1/2) trials. The number of trials T until (and including) the 3rd success has E[T] equal to
Four married couples sit around a circular table so that spouses sit together (each couple occupies two adjacent seats). Treating rotations as the same, the number of seating arrangements is _____.
questions.sol: Treat each couple as a block: 3! circular block arrangements, and each block can be ordered 2 ways: 6*16=96.

questions.stem: Joint density f(x,y)=8xy on the triangle 0<y<x<1. Then P(Y < 1/2) equals _____ (four decimals).
questions.sol: Integrate 8xy over y<1/2 inside the triangle: x in (0,1/2] with y<x plus x in (1/2,1] with y<1/2, giving 1/16+3/8=0.4375.

questions.stem: Among donors, 40% are type A, 10% type B, 50% type O. A mistyped record lists a donor as type A with probability 0.9 if truly A, 0.05 if B, 0.05 if O. Given a listed-A record, P(true type A) equals _____ (two decimals).
A mixed distribution: with probability 0.4, X~Bernoulli(0.5); with probability 0.6, X is identically 1. Then E[X] equals _____ (two decimals).
Among 6 independent TCP packets, each is lost with probability 0.2. The expected number of lost packets is _____ (one decimal).
A random variable X has MGF M(t)=exp(5t + 8 t^2). Then X is
questions.sol: Normal MGF exp(mu t + sigma^2 t^2 / 2) so sigma^2/2=8, sigma^2=16, mu=5.

questions.stem: Using inclusion-exclusion, the number of integers from 1 to 100 that are divisible by 2 or 3 or 5 is _____.
On the unit square with uniform joint density, P(Y > X+0.5) equals _____ (three decimals).
questions.sol: The region is a right triangle of legs 0.5, area 0.125.

questions.stem: Radar: an object is an aircraft with prior 0.05, else a bird. The radar alarm sounds with probability 0.99 on aircraft and 0.10 on birds. Given an alarm, P(aircraft) equals _____ (two decimals).
X given Y=y is Exponential with mean y, and Y is Exponential with mean 2. Then E[X] equals _____ (integer).
Each day of a 7-day week is rainy independently with probability 0.3. P(no rainy day) equals _____ (rounded to three decimals).
Quantile: X~Exp(rate=ln 2) so median m satisfies P(X<=m)=1/2. Then m equals
questions.sol: Survival e^{-(ln 2) m}=1/2 => (ln 2) m = ln 2 => m=1.

questions.stem: The number of integer solutions of w+x+y+z=8 with each variable >=0 and w>=2 is _____.
If f(x,y)=e^{-x-y} for x>0,y>0, then P(X+Y <= 1) equals 1-2/e. Numerically this is _____ (rounded to two decimals).
A student knows the answer with probability 0.7, otherwise guesses uniformly among 4 options. Given a correct response, P(the student knew it) equals _____ (two decimals).
Each of 12 students passes a qualifier independently with probability 0.8. The expected number who pass is _____ (one decimal).
Paired t-test vs two-sample t-test: 12 students measured before and after a workshop. The appropriate 1-sample analysis is a t-test on
options: the 12 differences, with 11 degrees of freedom
questions.sol: Pairing reduces to a one-sample t on differences; df=n-1=11.

questions.stem: A 4-person working group is chosen from 9 researchers and then one of the 4 is designated chair. The number of possible (group, chair) outcomes is _____.
Joint density f(x,y)=8xy on 0<y<x<1. The marginal f_X(x) for x in (0,1) is 4x^3. Hence f_X(1/2) equals _____ (one decimal).

Packets drop due to congestion (prior 0.6) or due to a link fault. A monitor reports 'congestion-like' with probability 0.8 under congestion and 0.3 under fault. Given that report, P(congestion) equals _____ (two decimals).
A sample of size 5 has values 1,2,3,4,100. Compared with the mean, the median is
options: 3, and it is far less affected by the 100
questions.sol: Median is 3. Mean is 22. The outlier inflates the mean.

questions.stem: From 10 distinct papers, 3 are chosen for an oral exam and then ordered (first, second, third). The number of possible ordered triples is _____.
Using the same joint table P(X=1,Y=1)=0.10, P(X=1,Y=2)=0.20, P(X=2,Y=1)=0.30, P(X=2,Y=2)=0.40, the value of P(Y=1|X=1) is _____ (rounded to two decimals).

At customs, 5% of travellers carry undeclared goods. A scanner alarms with probability 0.92 if undeclared goods are present and 0.08 otherwise. Given an alarm, P(undeclared goods) equals _____ (two decimals).
An ANOVA-free chi-squared: a spinner with 4 labelled faces is spun 40 times. Under fairness each expected count is 10. If all observed counts equal 10, the Pearson statistic is
options: 0, and one does not reject fairness

questions.stem: The multinomial coefficient 6!/(2!2!2!) counts the number of words of length 6 with two A's, two B's and two C's. Its value is _____.
A tumour is present with prior 0.01. An MRI is positive with probability 0.95 if a tumour is present and 0.02 otherwise. Given a positive MRI, P(tumour) equals _____ (two decimals).
Let X~Binomial(n,p) and Y~Poisson(np) with the same mean. Which comparisons are correct for 0<p<1, n>=2?
options: X and Y are equal almost surely
P(X=0)=(1-p)^n which is not equal to e^{-np} in general
questions.sol: Poisson has the larger variance np vs np(1-p). They are different laws; Poisson is a limit, not an a.s. identity.

questions.stem: A robot on a grid may move only right or up. The number of shortest paths from (0,0) to (4,3) is _____.
questions.sol: Need 4 right and 3 up, in some order: C(7,3)=35.

questions.stem: Lots: 90% of lots are good (defect rate 1%) and 10% are bad (defect rate 20%). One item drawn from a random lot is defective. P(the lot is bad) equals _____ (two decimals).
A data set of 7 distinct numbers is summarised. Which are true?
options: The sample mean is sensitive to that largest value
Changing the largest value does not change the median
The unique mode of 7 distinct numbers is the largest
The sample median is the 4th order statistic
questions.sol: For odd n the median is the middle order statistic, robust to extremes. With all values distinct there are 7 modes (or none unique), not 'the largest'.

questions.stem: A password is a length-4 string over {A,B,C,D,E} with no two consecutive characters equal. The number of such passwords is _____.
questions.sol: First char 5 choices; each later char has 4 choices (not equal to previous): 5*4^3=320.

questions.stem: A login failure is a brute-force attack with prior 0.15, else a user typo. An anomaly score is high with probability 0.88 on attacks and 0.12 on typos. Given a high score, P(attack) equals _____ (two decimals).
Let F be the CDF of Uniform(0,1). Which are true?
options: F is differentiable at 0.3 with derivative 1
F(x)=0 for x<0, F(x)=x for x in [0,1], F(x)=1 for x>1
questions.sol: Continuous uniform CDF is continuous (no jumps) and has density 1 on (0,1).

questions.stem: A 9-match season is split into 4 wins, 3 draws, 2 losses. The number of result sequences is 9!/(4!3!2!) = _____.
Three fair coins. Let T = at least two heads and W = at least one tail. P(T n W) equals _____ (three decimals).
questions.sol: T n W is exactly two heads (three heads has no tail). Probability 3/8=0.375.

questions.stem: The number of derangements of 4 distinct recommendation letters into 4 envelopes (no letter in the matching envelope) is _____.
Order statistics: 3 i.i.d. Uniform(0,1). E[max] equals 3/4 = _____ (two decimals).
The number of ways to distribute 7 identical USB sticks to 3 distinct interns (each may get zero) is _____.
3 i.i.d. Uniform(0,1). E[min] equals 1/4 = _____ (two decimals).
A 6-character OTP is formed from digits 0-9 with all characters distinct. The number of possible OTPs is _____.
A hypergeometric flavour without the name: an urn has 5 red and 7 blue tokens. Three tokens are drawn without replacement. P(all red) = C(5,3)/C(12,3) equals _____ (rounded to three decimals).
In a workshop of 12 people, every pair shakes hands exactly once. The number of handshakes is _____.
A coupon-collector with 4 coupon types, uniform independent draws. Expected draws to complete the set is 4(1+1/2+1/3+1/4) = _____ (one decimal).
Skewness of N(mu, sigma^2) is 0. For Exp(rate=1) the skewness E[(X-1)^3]/1^3 equals 2. The difference (Exp skewness minus Normal skewness) is _____.
A 2x2 covariance matrix [[4, 1], [1, 9]] has Corr(X,Y) equal to 1/(2*3) = _____ (rounded to two decimals).
Which of the following are subspaces of R^3?
questions.sol: Must contain 0 and be closed under addition. The product constraint is not a subspace; the affine plane misses 0.
The first two vectors already form a basis.

questions.stem: Which sets in R^3 are linearly independent?
questions.sol: A scalar multiple pair is dependent; the zero vector kills independence.

questions.stem: Any two bases of a finite-dimensional vector space

Arad to Bucharest, h(Arad)=366, a step Arad-Sibiu cost 140, h(Sibiu)=253. A* f(Sibiu) via Arad is
Quiescence search extends the horizon in tactical lines to reduce
options: horizon-effect blunders on captures just beyond the depth limit
questions.sol: Continue while the position is noisy.

questions.stem: MAX-MIN leaves 5,0 | 1,1. Root value max(min(5,0),min(1,1))= ____.
MAX-MIN leaves 5,0 | 1,1. Best first move is
Alpha starts at -inf, beta at +inf. After MAX sees a child value 4, alpha becomes ____.
MAX root children are terminals 8, -2, 5. Best move value is ____.
In alpha-beta, the pair (alpha,beta) at the root starts at
Depth-1 MAX with three terminals 2, 7, -4. After examining 2 then 7, alpha is ____.
Ephemeral : Fleeting :: Perennial : ________
questions.sol: Ephemeral and fleeting are synonyms; perennial pairs with enduring.

questions.stem: A two-digit number is 7 times the sum of its digits, and the tens digit is 3 more than the units digit. The number is
questions.sol: Let tens=u+3. Then 10(u+3)+u=7(u+3+u) gives 11u+30=14u+21 so u=3 and the number is 63.

questions.stem: Five people P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row facing north. P is second to the left of R. Q sits immediately right of P. T occupies an end. S is not at an end. R sits in the middle. Who is at the right end?
questions.sol: The unique row is P, Q, R, S, T, so T is at the right end.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 6. The ratio of the hexagon's area to the circle's area is
Miser : Hoard :: Spendthrift : ________
questions.sol: A miser hoards money; a spendthrift squanders it.

questions.stem: The product of the digits of a two-digit number is 18, and the number is 6 times its units digit. The number is
questions.sol: 10a+b=6b and ab=18 give 10a=5b so b=2a. Then 2a^2=18, a=3, b=6: the number is 36.

questions.stem: Six colleagues A,B,C,D,E,F sit around a circle. A sits opposite D. B sits immediately clockwise from A. C sits opposite E. Who sits opposite B?
questions.sol: With A at a seat and D opposite, B clockwise from A forces F opposite B.

questions.stem: A 3x3x3 cube is painted on all faces and cut into 27 unit cubes. The number of unit cubes with no paint is ________.
questions.sol: Only the inner cube is unpainted.

questions.stem: Scalpel : Surgeon :: Gavel : ________
questions.sol: A scalpel is the surgeon's tool; a gavel is the judge's.

questions.stem: A two-digit number plus its reverse is 110, and the tens digit exceeds the units digit by 4. The original number is
questions.sol: 11(a+b)=110 so a+b=10, and a-b=4, hence a=7, b=3: 73.

questions.stem: Pointing to a woman, a man says: 'Her mother's only brother is my father's only son.' The man has no brother. The woman is the man's
questions.sol: The man is the woman's maternal uncle, so she is his niece.

questions.stem: A 6x6x6 cube is painted on all faces and diced into unit cubes. The number of unit cubes with paint on exactly three faces is ________.
questions.sol: Only the eight corners have three faces painted.

questions.stem: Oasis : Arid expanse :: Archipelago : ________
questions.sol: An oasis is a wet patch in an arid expanse; an archipelago is a cluster of islands in an ocean.

questions.stem: A three-digit number has distinct positive digits in arithmetic progression with common difference 2. The number is 26 times the sum of its digits. The number is ________.
A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. Then A is E's
questions.sol: D is A's grandfather, so E is A's great-grandmother.

questions.stem: A 6x6x6 cube is painted on all faces and diced into unit cubes. The number of unit cubes with no paint is ________.
Lethargy : Vigour :: Apathy : ________
questions.sol: Lethargy is the lack of vigour; apathy is the lack of concern.

questions.stem: The units digit of 7^2025 is
questions.sol: Units of powers of 7 cycle 7,9,3,1. Since 2025 mod 4=1, the units digit is 7.

questions.stem: If 1 is opposite 6, 2 opposite 5, and 3 opposite 4 on a cube, and 4 is on top while the four side faces clockwise from the front are 2, 1, 5, 6, then the bottom face is
questions.sol: The four sides use 2,1,5,6, so remaining face 3 is opposite the top 4.

questions.stem: A 6x6x6 cube is painted on all faces and diced into unit cubes. The number of unit cubes with paint on exactly one face is ________.
questions.sol: Each of 6 faces contributes a 4x4 block of centre-face cubes: 96.

questions.stem: Alleviate : Aggravate :: Pacify : ________
questions.sol: Alleviate is the opposite of aggravate; pacify is the opposite of provoke.

questions.stem: The remainder when 3^25 is divided by 5 is
questions.sol: Powers of 3 mod 5 cycle 3,4,2,1. 25 mod 4=1, so the remainder is 3.

questions.stem: A cube net is a row of four squares with one square attached to the second square's top edge and one attached to the third square's bottom edge. This net
options: folds only to a cuboid that is not a cube
questions.sol: This hexomino is a standard valid cube net.

questions.stem: Six unit squares in a single row of length 6 are used as a net. This net folds to a cube?
options: only if one square is removed
questions.sol: A strip of six squares overlaps when folded; it is not a cube net.

questions.stem: Cartographer : Charts of land :: Lexicographer : ________
questions.sol: A cartographer compiles maps; a lexicographer compiles dictionaries.

questions.stem: The number of 3-digit positive integers whose digits sum to 4 is ________.
questions.sol: Let hundreds=1+x with x>=0. Then x+y+z=3 in non-negative integers, C(3+2,2)=10, and each part is at most 9 automatically.

questions.stem: Four colleagues F, G, H, J each teach exactly two of Algebra, Botany, Coding. Algebra is taught by F, G and H. Botany is taught by F and J only. Who teaches Coding but not Algebra?
questions.sol: F already has two courses. J must add Coding to Botany. G and H add Coding to Algebra. Only J teaches Coding without Algebra.

questions.stem: A plus-shaped net of five squares plus a sixth square attached to an outer edge of one arm
options: is a cube net for some attachments and not others
questions.sol: The extra square must not cause overlap; some attachments work.

questions.stem: Opaque : Light :: Dielectric : ________
questions.sol: An opaque body does not transmit light; a dielectric does not conduct electric charge.

questions.stem: The sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ... has next term
questions.sol: The terms are n(n+1) for n=1,2,3,... so the sixth is 6*7=42.

questions.stem: Four players Ami, Bo, Cy, Di each play exactly two of Go, Hex, Yote. Ami and Bo both play Go. Cy does not play Hex. Di plays Hex and Yote. Who else besides Ami and Bo plays Go?
questions.sol: Di skips Go. Cy skips Hex so Cy plays Go and Yote.

questions.stem: A right circular cylinder of radius 3 and height 4 is unrolled. The lateral surface is a rectangle of sides
questions.sol: The circumference 6*pi is one side; the height 4 is the other.

questions.stem: Dearth : Shortage :: Plethora : ________
questions.sol: Dearth means shortage; plethora means surplus.

questions.stem: Terms of 1, 2, 6, 15, 31, 56 follow adding successive squares. The next term is

Five positive integers have unique mode 5 (appearing twice), median 7, mean 8, and all entries other than the two 5s are distinct and different from 5 and 7. The number of such lists, up to order, is ________.
questions.sol: Sorted lists are 5,5,7,a,b with a+b=23 and 8<=a<b, giving four pairs.

questions.stem: A cone of slant height 5 and base radius 3 is unrolled. The sector's arc length is
questions.sol: The arc equals the base circumference 6*pi.

questions.stem: Novice : Seasoned craft :: Pauper : ________
questions.sol: A novice lacks seasoned craft; a pauper lacks affluence.

questions.stem: A geometric progression has first term 3 and ratio 2. An arithmetic progression has first term 5 and common difference 3. The 4th geometric term minus the 4th arithmetic term equals ________.
The unique 4-digit perfect square whose first two digits are equal and whose last two digits are equal is ________.
questions.sol: 88^2=7744 is the only 4-digit square of form AABB.

questions.stem: A square piece of paper is folded once along a diagonal and a small hole is punched through both layers near the midpoint of a short folded edge. Unfolded, the number of holes is
questions.sol: One fold gives two layers, hence two holes after unfolding.

questions.stem: Archaeology : Buried settlements :: Paleontology : ________
questions.sol: Archaeology studies buried settlements; paleontology studies fossils.

questions.stem: The pattern 2, 3, 8, 27, 112, ... multiplies by n and then adds n. The next term is
Letters stand for distinct digits and I+I=ME with ME a two-digit number. The value of I+M+E is ________.
questions.sol: 5+5=10, so I=5, M=1, E=0 and the sum is 6.

questions.stem: A cube has faces painted so that opposite faces share a colour (three colours, each used twice). After a rotation that brings a red face to the bottom, the top face is
questions.sol: Opposite faces stay opposite under rotation, so the new top is the other red face.

questions.stem: Cacophony : Discordant :: Euphony : ________
questions.sol: Cacophony is discordant sound; euphony is harmonious sound.

questions.stem: If every term after the second of 4, 10, 28, 82, ... equals 3 times the previous minus 2, the fifth term is
A three-digit palindrome with middle digit 6 equals 11 times a two-digit number. The palindrome is ________.
Four unit cubes are joined face-to-face in a straight tetromino (1x4). The surface area of the solid is
Flock : Geese in flight :: Shoal : ________
questions.sol: Geese gather as a flock; fish gather as a shoal.

questions.stem: The 5th term of 2, 5, 10, 17, ... (adding successive odd integers starting at 3) is ________.
questions.sol: Differences 3,5,7, then 9: 17+9=26. Equivalently n^2+1 at n=5 is 26.

questions.stem: In a class of 40, 25 take maths, 20 take physics, and 10 take both. The number who take neither is ________.
A regular tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces. The number of edges is
Telescope : Far-off objects :: Microscope : ________
questions.sol: A telescope reveals far-off objects; a microscope reveals minute specimens.

questions.stem: A mixed series is 5, 10, 20, 35, 55, ... The missing 6th term is
Among 50 people, 30 drink tea, 25 drink coffee, and 10 drink both. The number who drink neither is ________.
A plane cuts a sphere through a circle of radius 6. If the sphere's radius is 10, the distance from the centre to the plane is
Traitor : Treason :: Patriot : ________
questions.sol: A traitor is defined by treason; a patriot is defined by allegiance.

questions.stem: In 3, 8, 15, 24, 34, 48 the intended pattern is n^2-1. The term that does not fit is
All poets are dreamers. Some dreamers are critics. Which conclusion must follow?
questions.sol: All poets are dreamers already yields that some dreamers are poets.

questions.stem: A 2x2x2 cube made of 8 unit cubes is painted outside and disassembled. The number of unit cubes with paint on exactly two faces is
questions.sol: Every unit cube is a corner, so each has three painted faces.

questions.stem: Brittle : Snap under load :: Ductile : ________
questions.sol: Brittle materials snap; ductile materials can be drawn into wire.

questions.stem: The value of log2(3)*log3(4)*log4(8) is ________.
No square is a circle. All circles are round. Which conclusion follows?
questions.sol: The converse of 'no square is a circle' is 'no circle is a square'.

questions.stem: A unit cube sits on a table. The number of faces not touching the table is
questions.sol: Five faces are not on the table.

questions.stem: Vaccine : Prevent infection :: Antidote : ________
questions.sol: A vaccine prevents infection; an antidote counters a poison.

questions.stem: If log2(x-1)+log2(x+1)=3 with x>1, then x equals
All maps are charts. No chart is a sketch. Some sketches are drafts. Which is valid?
questions.sol: Maps sit inside charts, which are disjoint from sketches.

questions.stem: Three unit cubes are stacked as a 1x1x3 tower. The exposed surface area, including the base sitting on a table (base not exposed), is
Anchor : Vessel at rest :: Foundation : ________
questions.sol: An anchor holds a vessel; a foundation holds a building.

questions.stem: If log3(x)=2 and log_x(y)=3, then y equals ________.
If the first two statements are true, which completion is correct? All mesas are plateaus. Some plateaus are inhabited. Therefore
questions.sol: Every mesa is a plateau, so some plateaus are mesas.

questions.stem: A regular octahedron has 8 faces. The number of vertices is
questions.sol: Dual of a cube: 6 vertices, 12 edges, 8 faces.

questions.stem: Sculptor : Chisel :: Calligrapher : ________
questions.sol: A sculptor works with a chisel; a calligrapher works with a nib.

questions.stem: The number of digits in 2^10 * 5^8, written in decimal, is
A pair jointly sufficient to decide whether a positive integer m is divisible by 6 is
questions.sol: Even and divisible by 3 together mean divisible by 6.

questions.stem: Eclipse : Hide a disc :: Illuminate : ________
questions.sol: An eclipse hides a disc; to illuminate is to reveal a surface.

questions.stem: If 2^{log2(9)} + 10^{log10(4)} = k, then k equals

Eight friends sit at a square table, two per side, all facing inward. K sits immediately clockwise from L, and K and L are on the same side. M sits on the opposite side from K. Seats on M's side number
questions.sol: Each side of the square table has two seats.

questions.stem: If intensity rises as faint to dim to murky, then cool to chilly to ________ is analogous.
questions.sol: The first triple grows darker; cool to chilly to frigid grows colder.

questions.stem: In a linear queue of six, X is ahead of Y, Y is not last, and exactly two people stand between X and Y. If X is in position 2 (front is 1), Y is in position
questions.sol: Two between X and Y with X at 2 puts Y at 5.

questions.stem: Pedantic : Minute rules :: Ostentatious : ________
questions.sol: Pedantic fuss is over minute rules; ostentatious fuss is over showy display.

questions.stem: If log_b(64)=2, then log_2(b) equals
If 'some machines are noisy' and 'all noisy things are distracting' are true, which must be true?
Hive : Colony of bees :: Rookery : ________
questions.sol: A hive houses a bee colony; a rookery houses breeding seals (or similar colonial nesters).

questions.stem: A list price is 25% above cost. A 10% discount is then given on the list price. The profit percent on cost is
questions.sol: Selling price = 1.25*0.90=1.125 times cost, so profit is 12.5%.

questions.stem: A, B, C, D sit in a circle facing the centre. A sits to the immediate left of B. C sits opposite A. Who sits opposite B?
questions.sol: Opposite of A's left-neighbour B is D, the remaining person, who sits opposite B.

questions.stem: Malleable : Beaten into sheets :: Viscous : ________
questions.sol: Malleable metal can be beaten into sheets; a viscous fluid flows sluggishly.

questions.stem: A vessel holds 40 L of milk. 8 L is removed and replaced by water; the same operation is repeated once more. Milk remaining, in litres, is
If 'P is the brother of Q' and 'R is the father of P', then Q is R's
questions.sol: R is parent of P, and P and Q are siblings, so Q is R's child.

questions.stem: Quisling : Collaborator :: Polyglot : ________
questions.sol: A quisling is a collaborator; a polyglot is a speaker of many tongues.

questions.stem: A population grows 10% in one decade and then falls 10% in the next. The net change over both decades is

Four houses in a row are red, blue, green, yellow (not necessarily in that order). The red house is left of blue. Green is at an end. Yellow is immediately right of red. Blue is not at an end. The leftmost house is
questions.sol: Green at an end, blue not at an end, red-yellow-blue as a block, red left of blue: the unique row is Green, Red, Yellow, Blue.

questions.stem: Tundra : Treeless cold plain :: Atoll : ________
questions.sol: Tundra names a treeless cold plain; atoll names a ring-shaped coral reef.

questions.stem: In a paper of T marks, a candidate scoring 45% fails by 15 marks, while another scoring 60% passes by 21. Then T equals
Kiran, Leela, Mira, Nisha like four sports: polo, squash, rowing, archery, one each. Kiran does not like polo. Leela likes rowing. Mira does not like squash or polo. Nisha likes polo. Mira likes
questions.sol: Nisha=polo, Leela=rowing. Mira skips squash and polo, so Mira=archery, Kiran=squash.

questions.stem: Ink : Fountain pen :: Graphite : ________
questions.sol: Ink is the writing medium of a fountain pen; graphite is that of a pencil.

questions.stem: A grocer uses a 900 g weight in place of 1 kg and sells at cost price. The profit percent is
questions.sol: He delivers 900 g for the price of 1000 g, so profit/cost=100/900=100/9 %.

questions.stem: A clock shows 3:15. The smaller angle between the hands, in degrees, is
questions.sol: Minute hand at 90, hour hand at 90+7.5=97.5; difference 7.5.

questions.stem: Hypothesis : Tentative claim :: Verdict : ________
questions.sol: A hypothesis is a tentative claim; a verdict is a settled judgment.

questions.stem: Successive discounts of 10% and 20% on a marked price are equivalent to a single discount of ________ percent.
If all Bloops are Razzies and all Razzies are Lazzies, then all Bloops are Lazzies. This argument is
Gesticulate : Hands :: Articulate : ________
questions.sol: To gesticulate is to express with hands; to articulate is to express in speech.

questions.stem: A's salary is 25% less than B's. B's salary is greater than A's by
questions.sol: If B=100, A=75, so B exceeds A by 25/75=1/3, i.e. 100/3 %.

questions.stem: Five boxes are stacked. P is above Q. R is immediately above P. S is at the bottom. T is not adjacent to S. Who is immediately above S?
questions.sol: S is bottom. T cannot sit on S, so the consecutive triple R-P-Q occupies the three seats above S with Q on S, and T is on top: T, R, P, Q, S.

questions.stem: Archive : Stored records :: Reservoir : ________
questions.sol: An archive stores records; a reservoir stores water.

questions.stem: A share price rises 50% on Monday and falls 50% on Tuesday. Relative to Friday's close, the net change is
Among J, K, L, M: J is taller than K. L is shorter than K. M is taller than J. The tallest is
By the time the auditor arrived, the clerk ________ the ledgers twice.
questions.sol: A completed action before a past point takes past perfect: had reconciled.

questions.stem: To pass a 250-mark paper, 40% is required. A candidate scores 85. The candidate fails by
questions.sol: Pass mark is 100, so the shortfall is 15.

questions.stem: A statement 'All birds fly' is falsified by a single flightless bird. The logical name of that counterexample pattern is closest to
options: universal claim defeated by one negative instance
questions.sol: A universal is false if one counterexample exists.

questions.stem: Neither the surveys nor the census ________ a decline in literacy.
questions.sol: With neither-nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject census (singular): shows.

questions.stem: An article is sold at 20% profit. If both cost and selling price rise by Rs 120, the profit percent becomes 10%. The original cost, in rupees, is
In a coded language TREE is USFF. Then LEAF is coded as
questions.sol: Each letter shifts +1: L->M, E->F, A->B, F->G.

questions.stem: If the committee ________ quorum last Monday, the motion would have passed.
questions.sol: A past counterfactual conditional needs had + past participle: had had quorum.

questions.stem: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, then A:B:C equals
questions.sol: Scale B to 12: A:B = 8:12 and B:C = 12:15, so A:B:C = 8:12:15.

questions.stem: A man walks 3 km north, 4 km east, then 3 km south. Distance from the start is
Each of the prototypes ________ tested under salt spray before shipment.
questions.sol: Each is singular, so the verb is was.

questions.stem: If 2A = 3B = 4C, then A:B:C equals
If 15 August of a year is a Friday, 16 September of the same non-leap year is a
questions.sol: From 15 Aug to 16 Sep is 32 days = 4 weeks + 4 days; Friday+4=Tuesday.

questions.stem: She insisted that the report ________ on her desk by noon.
questions.sol: Insist that takes the mandative subjunctive: be.

questions.stem: The number 720 divided in the ratio 2:3:4 gives the largest share equal to ________.
questions.sol: Parts sum to 9, so each part is 80 and the largest share is 4*80=320.

questions.stem: Three switches A,B,C control three lamps in another room, one-to-one but unknown. You may toggle in the first room, then visit the lamp room once. A strategy that identifies all three pairings uses the fact that a bulb can be
questions.sol: Leave one on long enough to heat, one on just now, one off; warmth is a third state.

questions.stem: The data ________ inconsistent with the claimed linear trend.
questions.sol: In scientific usage data is treated as plural: are.

questions.stem: A 16 L blend of milk and water is in the ratio 3:1. The litres of water that must be added to make the ratio 2:1 is ________.
questions.sol: Milk is 12 L, so water must become 6 L; 2 L is added.

questions.stem: A Venn diagram of two sets A,B with |A|=12, |B|=8, |A intersect B|=5 has |A union B| equal to
Hardly ________ the gates opened when the crowd surged in.
questions.sol: Hardly/scarcely is followed by had + subject + past participle.

questions.stem: A 500 g alloy is gold and copper in the ratio 3:2. The mass of gold, in grams, is ________.
questions.sol: Gold is 3/5 of 500 g, i.e. 300 g.

questions.stem: From 16, 18, 21, 24 the integer that is not a multiple of 3 is
The panel recommended him ________ the liaison officer.
questions.sol: Recommend X as Y is the standard collocation here; as is correct.

questions.stem: A and B are in the ratio 4:5. After A's quantity is raised by 25%, the new ratio A:B is
questions.sol: A becomes 5 parts against B's 5 parts, so 1:1.

questions.stem: A 3x3x3 cube is painted on all six faces and then diced into unit cubes. The number of unit cubes with paint on exactly two faces is ________.
questions.sol: Each of the 12 edges contributes one non-corner edge-centre cube with exactly two faces painted.

questions.stem: Between you and ________, the draft still needs a figure caption.
questions.sol: The object of a preposition is me, not I.

questions.stem: A finishes a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together they finish it in
If NORTH is coded as OPSUI, then SOUTH is coded as
questions.sol: Each letter shifts +1: S->T, O->P, U->V, T->U, H->I.

questions.stem: It is one of those errors that ________ even careful editors.
questions.sol: The relative that refers to errors (plural), so escape.

questions.stem: A and B take 12 days, A and C take 15 days, B and C take 20 days. The days A, B and C together take is ________.
questions.sol: Adding the three pair rates gives twice the triple rate equal to 1/5, so the triple rate is 1/10.

questions.stem: A is looking at B. B is looking at C. A is married, C is unmarried, B's status is unknown. The statement 'a married person is looking at an unmarried person' is
questions.sol: If B is unmarried then A (married) looks at B; if B is married then B looks at C (unmarried).

questions.stem: No sooner ________ the fuse replaced than the motor hummed again.
questions.sol: No sooner was X than Y is idiomatic with a simple past passive.

questions.stem: A is twice as efficient as B, and together they finish a job in 8 days. The days A alone would take is ________.
questions.sol: Rates 2k and k sum to 3k=1/8, so A's rate is 1/12.

questions.stem: Three people U, V, W. Exactly one always tells the truth. U says 'V is the truth-teller.' V says 'U is the truth-teller.' W says 'U is not the truth-teller.' The truth-teller is
questions.sol: U true would force V to be the truth-teller as well. V true would force U to be. So W is the sole truth-teller, and both U and V are false.

questions.stem: The chemist, along with two technicians, ________ the titration.
questions.sol: Along with does not pluralise the subject; chemist takes performs.

questions.stem: Pipe P fills a tank in 6 hours; pipe Q empties it in 8 hours. Hours needed to fill the empty tank with both open is ________.
A calendar shows that a month has five Mondays. The fewest days that month can have is
questions.sol: Five Mondays need at least 29 days (Monday start in a 29-day month).

questions.stem: I would rather you ________ the raw counts tonight.
questions.sol: Would rather + subject takes a past-tense form for present preference: submitted.

questions.stem: A, B, C take 6, 8 and 12 days alone. A and B work 3 days, then C finishes the rest. C works for
questions.sol: A+B do 3*(1/6+1/8)=21/24, leaving 1/8. C's rate is 1/12, so time is 1.5 days.

questions.stem: Scarcely a page ________ free of a misplaced modifier.
questions.sol: Scarcely a page is singular: was.

questions.stem: Three men can finish a job in 10 days, or six women can. Days that one man and one woman together take is ________.
questions.sol: A man does 1/30 per day and a woman 1/60, together 1/20.

questions.stem: The board had the contract ________ by an outside counsel.
questions.sol: Causative have + object + past participle: had the contract reviewed.

questions.stem: Speeds of two walkers are in the ratio 3:4. The ratio of times they take for the same road is
questions.sol: Time is inversely proportional to speed.

questions.stem: Whoever the committee chooses ________ to file a disclosure.
questions.sol: Whoever ... chooses is a singular clause and takes has.

questions.stem: A can do a job in 18 days, B in 24 days, C in 36 days. They start together; A leaves after 4 days, then B leaves after 2 more days. Days C still needs after that is
questions.sol: Four days of A+B+C finish 1/2. Two days of B+C finish 5/36. Remainder 13/36, so C needs 13 days.

questions.stem: Ten kilometres ________ a long walk in this heat.
questions.sol: A measure used as a single distance is singular: is.

questions.stem: Two pipes fill a cistern in 20 min and 30 min. A drain empties it in 15 min. With all three open, the cistern fills in
He spoke as though he ________ the laboratory himself.
questions.sol: As though referring to an unreal past uses had designed.

questions.stem: A tap fills a tank in 8 hours. After 3 hours a leak that empties a full tank in 12 hours opens. Further hours needed to fill from that moment are
questions.sol: 3/8 is already in. Remaining 5/8 at net 1/8-1/12=1/24 per hour takes 15 hours.

questions.stem: Many a researcher ________ overnight in that archive.
questions.sol: Many a + singular noun takes a singular verb: has stayed.

questions.stem: Simple interest on Rs 2000 at 5% per annum for 3 years is ________ rupees.
The number of outliers ________ after the filter was applied.
questions.sol: The number of is singular: was reduced. (A number of would be plural.)

questions.stem: Compound interest on Rs 1000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually, is ________ rupees.
Let the samples ________ at room temperature overnight.
The difference between CI and SI on Rs 5000 for 2 years at 10% per annum is ________ rupees.
questions.sol: For two years the gap is P*(r/100)^2 = 50.

questions.stem: Not only the abstract but also the captions ________ rewriting.
questions.sol: Not only ... but also agrees with the nearer subject captions: need.

questions.stem: A principal becomes 9/4 of itself in 2 years at annual compound interest. The rate percent per annum is
This is the first time she ________ a keynote abroad.
questions.sol: This is the first time takes present perfect: has delivered.

questions.stem: The years needed for a sum to double at 8% per annum simple interest is
The minutes of the meeting ________ yet to be signed.
